pv.purpose: The measured temperature on each faceplate: the largest type on the panel, Process Red with a glow.

sv.purpose: The target temperature under the PV, about half its size, in Setpoint Green.

readout.purpose: OUT and MODE values beside PV and SV in the PID window.

headline.purpose: The recipe name at the top of the recipe column, in capitals.

title.purpose: Vessel names on the faceplates, in capitals.

lamp-state.purpose: The state word on a lamp button: HEATING 62 %, RUNNING, OFF, DID NOT STOP.

button.purpose: Command labels such as TARGET, STOP, NEXT STEP and AUTO.

row.purpose: Recipe step titles; banner text and recipe book names speak in the same voice.

detail.purpose: Step temperatures and times, additions, the deviation line and the last-event line.

label.purpose: PV, SV, OUT and MODE tags, step status, LOG and the connection label, in capitals.

nav.purpose: Screen tabs, in capitals; 14px on a phone.

body.purpose: Regular-width Barlow for whole sentences only: notes, confirmation questions and toasts.

shadows.name: sunken-window
shadows.purpose: The black PID window, sunk into the faceplate, with a 1px black border.

shadows.name: pv-glow
shadows.purpose: text-shadow on the PV digits; removed when readings go stale.

shadows.name: sv-glow
shadows.purpose: text-shadow on the SV digits; removed when readings go stale.

shadows.name: element-glow
shadows.value: SVG filter: feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 3, merged under the source
shadows.purpose: A heating element in the rig drawing.

shadows.name: pressed-ring
shadows.purpose: The active half of the AUTO | MANUAL switch.

shadows.name: floating-list
shadows.purpose: The event log list that LOG opens.

shadows.name: toast
shadows.purpose: The toast. With the log list, the only lifted surfaces.

motion.name: hold-press
motion.purpose: Element Orange fill at 32% sweeps left to right while a heat, AUTO or recipe START button is held (pointer, Space or Enter). Letting go early starts nothing. Kept under reduced motion.

motion.name: pending-march
motion.purpose: The lamp strip while a command waits for CraftBeerPi. Stops under reduced motion.

motion.name: pipe-flow
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset -24 over 0.9s linear infinite (dashes 5px on, 19px off)
motion.purpose: White dashes along a pipe whose pump is confirmed running. Stops under reduced motion.

motion.name: link-blink
motion.purpose: The connection lamp when the link is lost; the lamp is then a hollow Alarm Red ring rather than a filled dot, so the change is one of shape as well as colour. Stops under reduced motion.

motion.name: coil-change
motion.purpose: The HERMS coil turning Wort Gold when the wort pump runs and the wort is drawn going through it.

components.name: Boil Power
components.description: Only on a kettle whose logic declares set_boil_power (the boil kettle on Scott's rig). A command button beside the BOIL ELEMENT lamp, as tall as the lamp, labelled with the level it sets and when that level is used: BOIL POWER 45 % over "used from 210.2 °F · change" in AUTO (BoilPower's boil power, used once the wort reaches the kettle's target, 210.2 °F in the Boil step, or BoilPower's Boil_Threshold when there is none), POWER 100 % over "used by hand · change" in MANUAL (the element's own level). The kettle's mode decides, not the recipe, so the "Ready to boil?" hold, in MANUAL, shows POWER. A running recipe step never locks it. Tapping it swaps the mode row for an editor shaped like the target editor: −5, −1, the value in Panel White, +1, +5, SET in Selection Blue and CANCEL; the button has a Selection Blue outline while it is open. SET is a tap, not a held press: it changes a level, it doesn't switch heat on. Scott asked for it back on 10 Nov 2026.

narrative.overview:
This is the screen on the front of a brewhouse control cabinet, made for one rig: Scott's electric three-vessel HERMS. Each vessel gets a faceplate like a hardware PID controller: a big red measured temperature (PV) over a smaller green target (SV) in a black window, plus element power (OUT) and MODE, with the vessel's temperature graph under them in the same window. The vessels appear once more as a clean line drawing, plumbed the way the rig is plumbed, each one under its own faceplate. The recipe runs down the left. The screen refuses the generic dashboard made of a card grid of numbers and toggle switches.

Everything is read from across a garage, through steam, often with wet hands. So the panel holds a few large things rather than many small ones: condensed capitals, numbers that fill their windows, buttons 62-72px tall, and a hint on each button saying what a press will do. Colour works like indicator lamps on real equipment: each hue has one job, and every state shown by a colour is also written in words. The dark slate panel is Scott's stated preference over a light theme, even though the garage is lit.

Scott has turned down dial gauges, plotting all three temperatures on one shared scale, and the shaded kettle pictures of an earlier version, which he called crude. A generic web-app look is what he named as the thing that would make a redesign feel wrong. This record describes layout B of the built mockup (`proposal/brew-day.html`, the default). Layout A (`?layout=a`: recipe on the right, steel kettle pictures, tabs along the bottom) is kept only for comparison and is not part of the system.
keyCharacteristics: Dark slate panel; flat surfaces separated by 1px borders and small steps of tone.
One PID faceplate per vessel: PV big and red, SV smaller and green, OUT and MODE beside them, and the vessel's own temperature graph underneath.
Controls topped by an 8px lamp strip, with the state also written on the button.
A line drawing of the rig whose pipes take their liquid's colour and move only while pumped.
Barlow Condensed capitals for everything printed on the panel; regular Barlow only for sentences.
Heat starts only on a held press, and every command answers at its own button.

rules.name: The Red Is Reserved Rule
rules.body: Red means the measured temperature (PV) or something gone wrong: an alarm, a failed command, a lost connection. Off and stop are never red; even ALL OFF is neutral at rest and warms to red only under the pointer.

rules.name: The Say It Twice Rule
rules.body: Colour never carries a state alone. Lamp strips come with words (HEATING 62 %, RUNNING, OFF, DID NOT STOP), banners come with an icon and a title, pumped pipes come with moving dashes and arrow-heads, and finished steps say "✓ DONE".

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue marks where you are and what you are choosing: the current tab, the current recipe step, the target and power editors and the focus ring. Blue never shows the state of equipment.

rules.name: The PV Leads Rule
rules.body: The PV is the largest thing on its faceplate, about twice the size of the SV, red above green. Never make them the same size and never swap the colours.

rules.name: The Cabinet Lettering Rule
rules.body: Everything printed on the panel (names, tags, buttons, numbers) is Barlow Condensed, with names, tags, tabs and button labels in capitals and spacing between 0.02em and 0.1em. Regular-width Barlow is only for sentences addressed to the brewer.

rules.name: The Steady Digits Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes (PV, SV, OUT, the clock, countdowns, event times) uses tabular figures, so the digits don't shift as they tick.

rules.name: The One Screen Rule
rules.body: On a monitor, everything needed to run the brew (faceplates, drawing, recipe, alarms, last event) is visible at once, without scrolling the page. When height runs short, the drawing gives it up first, down to 140px; the PV digits never shrink for it. Only a screen under about 900px tall scrolls, and then only a little.

rules.name: The Under Its Plate Rule
rules.body: Each vessel in the drawing sits directly under its own faceplate. The drawing is generated at the width of its box, with the vessels centred at one sixth, one half and five sixths of the width.

rules.name: The Shared Rows Rule
rules.body: When the faceplates sit side by side (900px and wider), they share row heights through a CSS subgrid of six rows (name, window, deviation line, lamp buttons, mode row, note), so the windows and button rows line up across all three vessels.

rules.name: The Lit, Not Lifted Rule
rules.body: Things look important because they are lit, not because they float. Glows belong to readings and to equipment that is on; panels and buttons never cast shadows.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Someone Else Rule
rules.body: A dashed outline on a see-through button means another controller is in charge of that device (the vessel's AUTO, or the mash tun's HERMS running the hot liquor tank). It still explains itself when tapped. Solid buttons are yours to press.

rules.name: The Held Heat Rule
rules.body: Switching heat on by hand (an element, a vessel's AUTO, the recipe's START) needs a press held for one second, by pointer or with Space or Enter. Letting go early starts nothing and says "Keep holding for one second." Starting a pump, and anything that switches off or stops, is one tap. Once started, a recipe changes targets and modes as its steps require, and skipping ahead to the next step asks first. Changing a level is not switching heat on: a new target, boil power or element power is set with a tap on SET after adjusting it, whether or not the element is heating, because turning a boil down to stop a boil-over has to be quick.

rules.name: The Answer At The Button Rule
rules.body: Every command shows what happened on the button that sent it: waiting (marching stripes, "SWITCHING ON…", "SENDING…"), done (the new state, and "confirmed" on the last-event line), or failed (a red outline and "DID NOT STOP · tap to try again", plus an alarm banner).

rules.name: The Say Why Rule
rules.body: A control that can't be used right now stays on screen. When tapped, it explains why in its faceplate's note line (cleared after six seconds), in the recipe column's note line, or in a toast.

rules.name: The Trend In The Window Rule
rules.body: A vessel's temperature history belongs in its own PID window, under the PV and SV it explains, on its own scale, with real gridline values and clock times. Never a separate chart panel, never one plot shared by the three vessels, never a bare sparkline. The three graphs always show the same span.

rules.name: The Pumped-Only Flow Rule
rules.body: A pipe shows its liquid's colour and moves only while CraftBeerPi reports its pump running, and only along the branches its hand valves are drawn open for (The Hand Valve Rule). Before a start is confirmed, and whenever the connection is lost, the pipe stays still and slate. CraftBeerPi can't see a pump's own override switch, so a pump that has one says so under its label instead of the drawing guessing.

rules.name: The Hand Valve Rule
rules.body: CraftBeerPi can't see the hand valves, so the drawing never claims to know them: it draws them as the recipe needs them and says so under the boil kettle ("VALVES ARE SET BY HAND", then "SHOWN FOR RECIRCULATING" or "SHOWN FOR STEP 4 (SPARGE)"). From the start of the step named for the runoff (a name starting Sparge, Fly Sparge, Batch Sparge, Continuous Sparge, Lauter or Runoff, the same test as the core's first-wort reminder) until the boil starts, including the hold at "Ready to boil?", the wort goes to the boil kettle and the HLT pump's water goes to the top of the mash tun: Scott fly sparges (9 Nov). That holds even while the mash tun's AUTO still runs the wort pump for the HERMS. At any other time, and with no recipe, the drawing shows recirculating. Open valves are hollow bowties, closed ones solid, and each says OPEN or CLOSED.

dos: Do give every vessel a PID faceplate: PV in Process Red (#ff4b3e) at about twice the size of the SV in Setpoint Green (#3ddc6f), in a black window, with OUT and MODE beside them.

Do put each vessel's temperature graph in its PID window under its PV and SV: PV red, SV green, OUT as an orange band, its own scale, and 10 MIN, 30 MIN and DAY beside it; tapping any graph steps all three to the next span.
Do top every equipment control with an 8px lamp strip and write the state on the same button: HEATING 62 %, RUNNING, OFF, DID NOT STOP.
Do require a one-second held press (pointer, Space or Enter) to switch on an element, a vessel's AUTO or the recipe, and make switching off and stopping a single tap.

Do keep the boil power beside the boil element, settable at any time, also while a recipe runs, with its level on the button and when that level is used under it (from the kettle's target in AUTO, by hand in MANUAL).
Do show each command's outcome on its own button: marching stripes while waiting, the new state once confirmed, a 2px red outline and "tap to try again" when it fails.
Do keep unavailable controls visible and explain why when they are tapped, in the note line (#ffd9a0) or a toast.
Do keep the recipe on the brew-day screen: down the left on a monitor, below the faceplates on narrower screens.
Do colour and animate a pipe only while its pump is confirmed running: cyan (#46b8ea) for hot liquor, gold (#e9b33b) for wort.
Do draw the hand valves as the recipe needs them and say so under the boil kettle ("VALVES ARE SET BY HAND"); CraftBeerPi can't see them.
Do grey out readings and show their age when the connection is lost, stop the pipes and pause the controls.
Do keep tap targets at least 44px tall: lamp buttons 72px and command buttons 62px on a monitor (66px and 56px when the screen is 1000px tall or less), 56px and 50px on a phone.
Do set vessel names, tags, tabs and button labels in Barlow Condensed capitals, and give every changing number tabular figures.
donts: Don't show vessel temperatures as dial gauges or needles; Scott turned them down.
Don't plot the three vessels' temperatures on one shared scale; Scott turned that down too.
Don't draw a graph without its scale and times, or move the graphs out of the faceplates into a panel of their own.
Don't draw the vessels as shaded or realistic steel kettles; the rig is a clean line drawing.
Don't make the SV as big as the PV, or swap their colours.
Don't fall back to a grid of cards with numbers and toggle switches, or anything else that looks like a generic web app.
Don't use red for off or stop. Red is the PV and faults; off is a dark grey lamp strip (#3a4856).
Don't let colour be the only sign of a state.
Don't let a single tap or click switch on an element, a vessel's AUTO or the recipe.
Don't put the boil power behind the element's button or lock it while a recipe step runs; Scott turns the boil down mid-recipe.
Don't switch to a light theme; the dark panel is Scott's stated preference.
Don't remove controls on a phone; the phone drops only the drawing.
Don't use blue for equipment state; blue is for where you are and what you are choosing.
